verses.1: And all the people gathered together as one, at the place that was in front of the gate of the water. They said to Ezra, the scribe, “Bring forth the book of Moses’ laws, which Jehovah commanded Israel.”
verses.2: And the priest Ezra brought the Torah before the people, from one person to another woman, so that everyone who could hear it would do so on the seventh day of the month.
verses.3: And it was called so in front of the great valley, which lies in front of the gate of the water, from the light to half the day. It was directed towards men, women, and those who understand. And all the people listened to the book of the Torah.
verses.4: And Ezer, the scribe, stood on top of the hill where those things were made. Beside him stood Matityah, Shemaiah, Urieh, Hilkia, and Maaseiah. To his right stood Pedaiah, Mishael, Ishmael, Malchiah, Chusham, and Chashbadana. They all remembered them.
verses.5: And Ezar opened the book to all the people, as if it were something that belonged to all the people. And when he opened it, all the people stood up.
verses.6: And Ezer blessed the LORD, the great God. And all the people answered in agreement, “Amen!” They bowed their heads in worship before the LORD.
verses.7: And He will save me, my children, and Sherebyah. Right side is Akub Shabtai; Hodiyah is the work of Klitaya. Azarya, Yozabad, Hanan, Plaia… And the people will understand the law. The people stand firm in their beliefs.
verses.8: And they wrote down in the book the words of God, along with their meanings. Then they understood what it meant.
verses.9: And Nehemiah said, “This is the Temple and Ezra, the priest, and the scribes. They are those who understand the people for all nations today. This is the Holy One of God, your God. Do not mourn or weep, for all the people are crying when they hear the words of the Torah.”
verses.10: And he said to them, “Go and eat unleavened bread, and drink water that is not yet fermented. Send gifts to those who are not worthy of them, for today is a holy day for our Lord. Do not be discouraged, for the LORD’s anger is upon you.”
verses.11: And the Levites shall say to all the people, “Be careful, for today is a holy day. Do not be discouraged.”
verses.12: And all the people went out to eat and drink, and to celebrate in great joy, because they understood what they were told.
verses.13: And on the second day, the leaders of the fathers gathered together all the priests and Levites at Ezra’s place. They came to hear what the Torah said.
verses.14: And they found a writing in the Torah, which commanded that Moses should give this commandment to the children of Israel during the seventh month.
verses.15: And when they shall sound the trumpet, and proclaim it in all their cities and in Jerusalem, they shall say, “Come down from the mountains, and bring down wood, along with branches from the trees of Lebanon, and from other trees as well. Use these materials to make sticks, just as it is written.”
verses.16: And the people went out and made altars for themselves on their roofs, in their courtyards, in the courtyards of the Temple, and also in the areas around the gates of the city.
verses.17: And all the people who returned from captivity made tabernacles. They settled in those tabernacles, for since the days of Joshua son of Nun, and even until today, the children of Israel have not done so like this. And there was great joy among them.
verses.18: And he wrote down in the book of God’s laws, from one day to another. They celebrated a seven-day holiday. On the eighth day, they observed a rest according to the law.
